title: Awareness of African roots and Cuban freedom
summary: Young Afro-Cubans were aware of Africa; he talks about enthusiasm for freedom after the war with Spain.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I see now that as a young, a young man growing up, you were very aware of your African roots. Were the other Afro-Cubans aware of it also?

Definetely. It was no way out. We was in the same neighborhood like a - ah - let's call it ghetto, where people just getting to be like a one-track mind, just enjoy themselves, get whatever is left.......
No, but what I am driving at Macho, is that all the young Afro-Cubans there were aware of Africa and their roots.
Were there any that didn't want to know about it and just wanted to say I am Cuban, I only want to know about what's happening here now.

There was just few, because in account of my time, my age, that was almost the beginning of the country and eawrybody was celebrating the freedom, helped by the United States, there is no question about it, otherwise we still been fighting in Cuba with the Spanish because it was a big country.

So that combination of the declaration of the war in America to Spain; Spain knew that they are going to lose with United States because the United States was so close. So they give up Cuba, they give up Puerto Rico and Philippines and so forth and so on. So everybody was so enthusiastic about the freedom and about and enjoying what we what was Spaniard because we respect all the property, everything that the Spanish has out there. I think it is the only country in the world that had freedom from one particular country and respects its property. We respect everything that they has.
